## Teaching points

1. Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (schistocytes, high LDH, low haptoglobin, indirect hyperbilirubinemia, reticulocytosis, negative DAT) with severe thrombocytopenia is TTP until proven otherwise.
2. Near-normal PT, aPTT and INR help separate TTP from DIC; severe thrombocytopenia with only mild kidney injury favors TTP over HUS.
3. ADAMTS13 results take days: a PLASMIC score of 6–7 supports starting plasma exchange and corticosteroids at once (ISTH 2020 TTP guidelines); delays beyond 24 h are linked to higher mortality.
4. Neurological signs in TTP fluctuate, and a normal CT does not exclude microvascular ischemia.
5. Platelet transfusion is generally avoided unless bleeding is life-threatening; rituximab and caplacizumab are adjuncts in immune TTP.
